Heard Smt.Sushmitha.G, learned counsel who represents Sri.N.Gopal Krishna, learned counsel for
the appellants as well as Sri.S.Krishna Kishore, learned counsel for respondent No.2-Insurance
Company.
2.

Challenge in this appeal is the order that is rendered by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, NC:
2024:KHC:32788 Bengaluru in MVC No.6397/2016 dated 27.07.2018.

sentences.text: The appellants as claimants filed a petition claiming compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- in total.
The Tribunal through the impugned order awarded a sum of Rs.3,70,000/- as compensation and aggrieved by the same, the present appeal is preferred.
3. On hearing both the learned counsel and upon perusing the relevant material that is brought on record, the following undisputed facts are found:

( a) The husband of the first appellant and father of appellant Nos.2 and 3 i.e.,
D.Krishnappa died in the road traffic accident that occurred on 23.06.2016.

(b) The deceased D.Krishnappa was aged about 68 years by the date of accident.

sentences.text: (c) The deceased worked as an employee in Syndicate Bank and retired from service.
(d) The deceased D.Krishnappa was getting Rs.16,800/- p.m. as pension by the date of his death.
NC: 2024:KHC:32788 (e) The first appellant being the wife of the deceased D.Krishnappa is getting Rs.7,000/- p.m. as pension after the death of her husband D.Krishnappa.
4. Arguing the matter, Smt.Sushmitha.G contends that the deceased was holding agricultural land by the date of accident and he was getting agricultural income.
All the appellants were depending upon the earnings of the deceased by the date of accident.
However, the Tribunal assessed the notional income of the deceased as Rs.10,000/- p.m. only which is erroneous.
Learned counsel also states that the Tribunal held that the appellant Nos.2 and 3 who are major sons of the deceased cannot be considered to be the dependents of the deceased which is incorrect.

Learned counsel submits that all the appellants were depending upon the earnings of the deceased by the date of accident and therefore, taking into consideration the agricultural income of the deceased and holding that even the major sons i.e., appellant Nos.2 and 3 are dependents of the deceased,
justifiable amount may be NC: 2024:KHC:32788 granted under the head loss of dependency.
Learned counsel also states that a sum of Rs.40,000/- is awarded under the head loss of consortium which is inadequate.

5. Vehemently opposing the submission thus made, Sri.S.Krishna Kishore, learned counsel for respondent No.2 submits that the appellant Nos.2 and 3 who are the major sons of the deceased are not entitled for any compensation under the head loss of dependency.
Indeed they were not depending upon the earnings of the deceased.
Learned counsel brought to the notice of this Court the evidence of Pw.1 and her statements given in cross examination.

Learned counsel submits that Pw.1 i.e., appellant No.1 clearly stated in her cross examination that one of her son is an employee in Municipal Corporation and the other son is working in a Private Company.
She also stated that both are married.

Learned counsel submits that when the sons are employed, residing separately, are eking out their livelihood and are also maintaining their family members i.e., their wives and NC:
2024:KHC:32788 children, they cannot be considered to be the dependents of the deceased.
This Court is of the view that the submission thus made requires consideration.
No evidence whatsoever is produced by the appellants 2 and 3 that they were depending upon the earnings of the deceased by the date of accident.

Therefore, this Court holds that there is nothing to interfere with the finding given by the Tribunal that the appellant Nos.2 and 3 who are the major sons of the deceased cannot be considered to be the dependents of the deceased.

6. Coming to the income of the deceased, though Ex.P11-RTC extracts are produced and they show that agricultural land stands in the name of the deceased, no proof is produced with regard to the earnings of the deceased through agriculture.
The Tribunal assessed the income of the deceased notionally as Rs.10,000/- p.m.
The said figure is highly justifiable.

Applying the appropriate multiplier, the Tribunal came to a conclusion NC: 2024:KHC:32788 that an amount of Smt Lakshmidevamma vs Sri Venkatesh G on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34679446/
3 Rs.3,00,000/- is required to be awarded under the head loss of dependency.

sentences.text: 7. The Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.40,000/- only under the head loss of consortium.

However,
appellant No.1 being the wife of the deceased is entitled to Rs.40,000/- towards loss of spousal consortium and the appellant Nos.2 and 3 being the sons of the deceased are entitled to Rs.40,000/-
under the head loss of parental consortium.

Therefore, the appeal is required to be allowed to that extent enhancing compensation by Rs.40,000/-.
8.

Thus the following:
ORDER (i) Appeal is allowed in part.
(ii) The amount that is awarded as  compensation by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Bengaluru through orders in MVC No.6397/2016 dated 27.07.2018 is enhanced by Rs.40,000/-.
NC: 2024:KHC:32788 (iii) The enhanced amount shall carry interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
(iv) Respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the enhanced sum within a period of 8(eight) weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order.
(v) The appellant Nos.2 and 3 are entitled to equal share out of the enhanced sum.
are permitted to withdraw their respective shares.
